report.summary: Two product bugs in app/main.py cause all three failures. First fix the book-list data leak: list_books() ignores user_id, so one user sees other users' books (api test_users_cannot_see_each_others_books). Second fix the year validation: validate_book() accepts next year (this_year + 1) while its own error message says the maximum is this year, which fails both the API next-year test and the UI future-year test.

causes.title: GET /api/books returns every user's books
causes.explanation: list_books(user_id) never uses user_id. The query selects all rows from books, so any authenticated user receives every book in the database. Ownership is enforced for get, update and delete (get_own_book filters by owner_id), so the leak is limited to listing. The same function also feeds the /books page via render_books, so the UI leaks the same data. The failure is deterministic: the test creates a book as one user and the other user's list contains its id.
evidence: tests/api/test_books_api.py:42: assert book["id"] not in other_ids -> AssertionError: assert 2 not in [1, 2]
app/main.py:147-150: def list_books(user_id: int) -> list[dict]: ... rows = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM books ORDER BY id").fetchall()
app/main.py:163-170: get_own_book filters with "WHERE id = ? AND owner_id = ?", so only the listing lacks the owner filter
causes.suggested_fix: Change the query in list_books to "SELECT * FROM books WHERE owner_id = ? ORDER BY id" and pass (user_id,). Add a test that a user's list excludes other users' books and run it against the UI page as well.

causes.title: Year validation accepts next year although the error message says the maximum is this year
causes.explanation: validate_book allows years up to this_year + 1 ("1 <= book.year <= this_year + 1"), but the error text it returns is "Year must be between 1 and {this_year}". The API therefore returns 201 for a year of next year, where the test expects 422. In the UI the same input is saved (the row 'Future-... Someone 2027' appears in the table) and no error element is rendered, so the test's wait for the error times out. The test expectations match the app's own message, so the code is most likely the part that is wrong. The one open question is whether next-year entries were meant to be allowed, in which case the message and both tests would need changing instead; the evidence does not settle that.
evidence: app/main.py:81-84: if book.year is not None: this_year = date.today().year; if not 1 <= book.year <= this_year + 1: raise HTTPException(422, f"Year must be between 1 and {this_year}")
tests/api/test_books_api.py:58 and 63-66: ({"title": "T", "author": "A", "year": THIS_YEAR + 1}, "Year must be between") ... assert response.status_code == 422
tests/api/test_books_api.py:47-50: test_current_year_is_accepted passes with THIS_YEAR, so the boundary is the only thing in question
UI error: Locator expected to contain text 'Year must be between' ... Actual value: None / Error: element(s) not found (get_by_test_id("error"))
UI aria snapshot lists row "Future-ea43e8ce Someone 2027 Delete", showing the next-year book was saved
causes.suggested_fix: Change the upper bound in app/main.py:83 to `book.year <= this_year` so it matches the message. This should make both the API test and the UI test pass. If next-year entries are intended, change the message and the test expectations instead, and confirm this with the product owner.
